title: Casserole
summary: One-dish baked comfort — French word, Midwest soul.
origins: From French cassole (earthenware pot). American casserole culture peaked mid-20th century: Campbell's soup recipes, church potlucks, and freezer-ahead family dinners. Minnesota hot dish is the regional dialect.
history: Depression-era and WWII rationing made one-dish meals practical. 1950s freezer marketing cemented tuna noodle and green bean formats. Modern remakes often deconstruct; originals were engineered for cans and convenience.
teaching: Undercook pasta slightly — it finishes in the oven.
Let rest 10 min after baking — sets the slice and saves your tongue.
Cover with foil first; uncover last 10 min for golden top.
fun_fact: Casserole comes from the French word for saucepan — one dish, zero drama.
